cards.alt: Sample multiple choice card: Multiple sclerosis most directly damages which cell type?

questions.stem: A patient develops ascending muscle weakness two weeks after a viral infection, and nerve conduction is slowed. Which cells are the most likely target?
questions.explanation: Guillain-Barre syndrome attacks PNS myelin, made by Schwann cells, which slows conduction. Oligodendrocytes make CNS myelin and are involved in multiple sclerosis. Astrocytes and microglia do not form myelin.

questions.stem: Which structure belongs to the PNS?
questions.explanation: The dorsal root ganglion lies outside the cord and holds sensory neuron cell bodies. The dorsal horn and central canal are inside the cord, and the corpus callosum is in the brain.
questions.subtopic: Organization of the nervous system (CNS, PNS)

questions.stem: A subject notices the difference between 100 g and 102 g. Using Weber's law, what difference is needed to notice a change from 400 g?
questions.explanation: The JND is a constant fraction (2 percent) of the baseline, so 400 g needs 8 g. A constant 2 g would ignore the baseline, and 4 g or 40 g use the wrong fraction.

questions.stem: After a head injury, a patient loses the sense of smell. What is the most likely damage?
options: The optic chiasm above the pituitary
Olfactory axons at the cribriform plate
The vagus nerve in the neck
The cochlear nerve in the inner ear
questions.explanation: Fine olfactory axons cross the cribriform plate to the olfactory bulb and can be sheared by trauma. The optic chiasm, vagus and cochlear nerve serve other senses.

questions.stem: A patient stops long-term prednisone abruptly and becomes weak and hypotensive. Why?
options: Suppressed ACTH had let the adrenal cortex atrophy
Excess aldosterone caused fluid volume overload
The adrenal medulla began producing cortisol
questions.explanation: Chronic glucocorticoid suppresses CRH and ACTH, leading to adrenal atrophy and cortisol deficiency when the drug stops. Aldosterone is usually preserved because it depends on RAAS, and the medulla does not make cortisol.

demo_cards.extra: Input at one end, output at the other.

demo_cards.stem: Multiple sclerosis most directly damages which cell type?
demo_cards.why: MS is autoimmune demyelination of the CNS, so the myelin-forming oligodendrocytes are the target. Schwann cells are hit in Guillain-Barre syndrome, which affects the PNS.

demo_cards.statement: A single Schwann cell myelinates segments of many different axons.
demo_cards.why: One Schwann cell wraps a single internode of one axon. Oligodendrocytes are the cells that wrap several axons.
